q: What emission factor should we use for kerosene?
title: Kerosene emission factor
short: Use the IPCC 2006 default for other kerosene: 71,900 kg CO2 per TJ at a net calorific value of 43.8 TJ per thousand tonnes, about 3.15 kg CO2 per kg. At a density near 0.8 kg per litre that is roughly 2.5 kg CO2 per litre; use your supplier's density if stated.
audience: Users of kerosene in heaters, lamps or cleaning

ul: Space heaters and lamps at remote sites.
Parts cleaning, if it is burned afterwards.

p: Kerosene burned in your equipment is Scope 1. Kerosene used only as a cleaning solvent and not burned is not combustion; see the solvent page.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site, and labels estimates as estimates.
